issues.legal_issue: A final determination under the statutory scheme of the amount recoverable from a jagirdar bars a later attempt to recover the same dues through ordinary revenue proceedings.
material_facts: The State claimed pre-resumption revenue dues from compensation payable to the jagirdar but did not provide a proper account or the particulars sought by the Jagir Commissioner.
After inquiry, the Jagir Commissioner determined that no amount was recoverable from the jagirdar on that claim and ordered that nothing be deducted from compensation.
The Board of Revenue dismissed the State’s appeal, and the State did not otherwise challenge those decisions under the statutory scheme.
The State later initiated proceedings to recover the same dues through the general revenue machinery.
The compensation payable to the jagirdar substantially exceeded the claimed liability, and the applicable rules provided for adjustment and further recovery of any remaining balance.
issues.conclusion: The determination by the Jagir Commissioner, affirmed by the Board of Revenue, was final. The later revenue recovery proceedings were without jurisdiction, and the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 22(1)(e), 30–35 and 39 of the Rajasthan Land Reforms and Resumption of Jagirs Act, 1952, together with rule 37-C(4) of the Rules, establish a comprehensive process to determine and recover dues from a jagirdar, including adjustment against compensation and recovery of any remaining balance. Under section 46, civil and revenue courts cannot deal with a matter required to be settled, decided or dealt with under the Act, and an order made under it cannot be called in question in court; section 47 gives the Act overriding effect over inconsistent laws. The statutory determination and appeal having become final, sections 229 and 257A of the Rajasthan Land Revenue Act could not be used to reopen the same claim. The cited decisions concerning other circumstances in which civil-court jurisdiction was not ousted were inapplicable.

rule.if: revenue_recovery_proceeding and same_dues_previously_determined and statutory_appeal_dismissed and determination_left_unchallenged and compensation_exceeds_claimed_liability

predicates.revenue_recovery_proceeding: A revenue authority initiates a later proceeding to recover dues from a person.
predicates.same_dues_previously_determined: An authorized decision-maker has already determined whether the same claimed dues are recoverable from that person.
predicates.statutory_appeal_dismissed: An appeal from that determination is dismissed.
predicates.determination_left_unchallenged: The determination and its appellate affirmance are not otherwise successfully challenged through the applicable process.
predicates.compensation_exceeds_claimed_liability: The compensation payable to the person exceeds the claimed liability, and the statutory process provides for adjustment and recovery of any balance.

issues.definition: When a revenue recovery proceeding concerns dues already finally determined through the applicable process, and the compensation exceeds the claimed liability, the later recovery proceeding is barred.

issues.legal_issue: An alleged prior resolution that was not produced in the statutory inquiry does not permit the State to disregard the resulting final determination of the dues.
material_facts: The State relied on an alleged earlier council resolution as establishing the jagirdar’s liability.
The State did not produce that resolution before the Jagir Commissioner when the claimed dues were investigated.
The jagirdar denied knowledge of or agreement to the resolution and disputed that the claimed dues were payable.
The Jagir Commissioner rejected the claim after inquiry, and the Board of Revenue dismissed the State’s appeal.
issues.conclusion: The alleged resolution did not establish a basis for treating the Jagir Commissioner’s determination as illegal or for disregarding it in later recovery proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 32 and 39 of the Rajasthan Land Reforms and Resumption of Jagirs Act, 1952, provide for determination of recoverable dues by the Jagir Commissioner and an appeal to the Board of Revenue, whose appellate decision is final. Section 46 bars a court from reopening a matter decided through that process. The Court rejected the contention about the council resolution because it had not been produced in the statutory inquiry and the resulting determination had become final.

rule.if: challenge_to_final_statutory_determination and alleged_prior_resolution_not_produced and liability_disputed and statutory_appeal_dismissed

predicates.challenge_to_final_statutory_determinati: A party seeks to avoid the effect of a final determination made through a statutory process.
predicates.alleged_prior_resolution_not_produced: The party relying on an alleged earlier resolution does not produce it during the statutory inquiry into the claimed liability.
predicates.liability_disputed: The person against whom liability is claimed disputes knowledge of or agreement to the alleged resolution and disputes the liability.
predicates.statutory_appeal_dismissed: An appeal from the statutory determination is dismissed.

issues.definition: When a final statutory determination is challenged on the basis of an alleged earlier resolution that was not produced in the inquiry, and the liability was disputed, dismissal of the statutory appeal leaves the determination undisturbed.
